issue.title: Bug: [smartswitch] gnoi-shutdown-daemon intermittently fails gNOI Reboot with connection refused during DPU shutdown

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

Intermittent failure when shutting down all DPUs via `config chassis shutdown DPUx`.
Some DPUs fail to send the gNOI Reboot HALT command.
There's a previous fix trying to solve this issue: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-host-services/pull/364
The log shows the error message still shows after the fix was merged.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. On SmartSwitch with N DPUs, run `config chassis shutdown DPU0` ... `DPU(N-1)` (or equivalent bulk shutdown)
2. Observe `gnoi-shutdown-daemon` logs on NPU

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

## Expected behavior
All DPUs receive gNOI Reboot HALT and shut down gracefully.

## Actual behavior
Some DPUs fail with connection refused to gNOI port.

### Relevant log output

```shell
debug message:
DPU1: Reboot command failed (rc=2, target=:50052): panic: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp :50052: connect: connection refused" ...

syslog:
NOTICE gnoi-shutdown-daemon[20022]: DPU1: Admin shutdown detected, initiating gNOI HALT
NOTICE gnoi-shutdown-daemon[20022]: DPU1: Starting gNOI shutdown sequence
NOTICE gnoi-shutdown-daemon[20022]: DPU1: PCI detach complete, proceeding for halting services via gNOI
ERR gnoi-shutdown-daemon[20022]: DPU1: Reboot command failed
ERR gnoi-shutdown-daemon[20022]: DPU1: Failed to send Reboot command
```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell

```

### Attach files (if any)

- gNOI server confirmed running on DPUs; gnmi_port aligned in CONFIG_DB
- `gnoi_client` panics on dial failure (reboot.go:21)

resolution.title: gnoi-shutdown: use per-thread DB connections to avoid crossed DPU reads
resolution.description:
### What I did
Fixes:https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28175
`gnoi-shutdown-daemon` spawns one worker thread per DPU on shutdown, but all threads shared a single CONFIG_DB/STATE_DB redis connection created once in `main()`. A redis `DBConnector` is a single, non-thread-safe socket, so when multiple DPUs shut down in parallel their `hget`/`Table` reads interleave on the wire and replies get matched to the wrong request — producing **crossed IP/port values between DPUs**.

This gave gnoi_client a bad target like `<IP>:<IP>` (dpu0's IP as host, dpu1's IP in the port slot), causing:

```
ERR gnoi-shutdown-daemon: DPU1: Reboot command failed (rc=2, target=<IP>:<IP>):
panic: rpc error: ... dial tcp: lookup tcp/<IP>: unknown port
```

### Fix
Give each per-DPU worker thread its own CONFIG_DB/STATE_DB connection so reads can never cross:
- `handle_and_cleanup()` opens fresh `db_connect("CONFIG_DB")` / `db_connect("STATE_DB")` per thread and passes them into `_handle_transition()`.
- `_handle_transition()` / `_wait_for_gnoi_halt_in_progress()` take optional per-thread connections, falling back to the shared ones for direct/unit-test callers (backward compatible).

### Testing
- `py_compile` clean.
- Smoke-tested both paths: per-thread connections are the ones actually used (correct `<IP>:50052`), and fallback-to-shared preserves existing unit-test behavior.
